Bitcoin just had its worst month since the 2022 crypto crash — and if you hold it in an app, an ETF or your brokerage, that's your money too.

Bitcoin is down about 21% in November, its steepest monthly drop since June 2022 (Moneycontrol; Bloomberg). It slipped below $60,000 for the first time since July before clawing back above $61,000. Investors pulled a record $3.79 billion out of U.S. Bitcoin ETFs this month — BlackRock's fund alone shed about $2.47 billion (Seeking Alpha; Cointelegraph).

My take: a 21% month is gut-wrenching, but the people who get hurt most are usually the ones who bought the top on hype and sell the bottom in fear.

Did this month's drop change how much crypto you're comfortable holding?
